headline: Shifts Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear a greater share of grid infrastructure costs, aiming to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocates, Governor Spanberger.
opponents: Large energy users, data center industry.
news_headline: Governor Unveils Data Center Accountability Framework, Lowers Energy Costs
news_summary: Governor Spanberger introduced a Data Center Accountability Framework, which includes measures to protect Virginians from higher energy bills by requiring data centers to pay for transmission infrastructure built exclusively for their operations. This initiative aims to ensure data center growth benefits communities without increasing residential energy costs.

headline: Mandates Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water providers to report the total volume of water supplied to data centers, increasing transparency on their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new state law mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, with numbers to be aggregated and available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide credible data on water consumption by the rapidly growing data center industry.

headline: Establishes Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill empowers localities to require site assessments for new large data centers, including sound profiles and potential impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites, before approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental advocates.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Virginia Law Requires Data Center Siting Assessments
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments, including sound profiles, for new facilities. While it mandates studies, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some discretion to local governments.
